claim: SQSTM1 is an adaptor protein that integrates multiple cellular signaling pathways.
source: SQSTM1 is an adaptor protein that integrates multiple cellular signaling pathways and whose expression is tightly regulated at the transcriptional and post-translational level.

claim: SQSTM1 expression is tightly regulated at the transcriptional and post-translational level.

claim: CRISPR is superior to RNAi in identifying known SQSTM1 modulators.
source: Through systematic comparison of pooled libraries, we show that CRISPR is superior to RNAi in identifying known SQSTM1 modulators.

claim: A genome-wide CRISPR screen exposed MTOR signalling as a key regulator of SQSTM1.

claim: Inhibition of autophagy with sgRNAs against the lipid kinase PIK3C3 robustly accumulated GFP-SQSTM1.

claim: MTOR sgRNAs were enriched in GFP low cells.

claim: MTOR and PIK3C3 sgRNAs did not significantly impair cell proliferation.

claim: Both CRISPR and RNAi identified many known modulators of SQSTM1, including MTOR, RPTOR, RB1CC1, BECN1, PIK3C3, ULK1 or ATG7.

claim: sgRNAs showed a tighter distribution than shRNAs when all CRISPR and RNAi reagents were analyzed in GFP high versus GFP low cells.

claim: MTOR, RPTOR and RHEB were among the top ranked genes in GFP low cells in the genome-wide screen.

claim: Depletion of MTOR, RPTOR and RHEB activates autophagy and induces degradation of SQSTM1.
source: By analyzing sgRNA sequences enriched in GFP low cells, we identified MTOR, RPTOR and RHEB among the top ranked genes, in line with their depletion activating autophagy and inducing degradation of SQSTM1 (Figure 2A).

claim: Several components of the mediator complex were observed among top ranked genes in GFP low cells.
source: We also observed several components of the mediator complex and an enrichment analysis of the top ranked 100 genes revealed transcriptional regulation by RNA polymerase II as significantly enriched GO biological process (Figure 2C).

claim: Transcriptional regulation by RNA polymerase II was a significantly enriched GO biological process among the top ranked 100 genes in GFP low cells.

claim: sgRNA sequences enriched in GFP high cells targeted many autophagy genes such as ATG9A, RB1CC1, ATG16L1, ATG7, ATG3, ATG5, WIPI2, MAP1LC3B and ATG14.

claim: The 5 sgRNA per gene in the genome-wide library performed equally well as the 20 sgRNAs per gene in the focused CRISPR library in identifying autophagy pathway components when the maximal fold change was analyzed per gene.
source: In comparison to the 20 sgRNAs per gene in the focused CRISPR library (Figure 1), the 5 sgRNA per gene in the genome-wide library performed equally well in identifying autophagy pathway components when the maximal fold change was analyzed per gene (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Autophagy pathway components which did not significantly score were restricted to genes which have functional homologs.
source: Autophagy pathway components which did not significantly score were restricted to genes which have functional homologs.

claim: ATG4A, ATG4C, ATG4D, ULK2, ATG16L2, WIPI1 and ATG9B were all inactive while their homologs ATG4B, ULK1, ATG16L1, WIPI2 and ATG9A robustly scored.

claim: A strong enrichment and connectivity signal was confirmed for autophagy and MTOR signaling pathways.
source: By analyzing subclusters of highly connected gene sets, a strong enrichment and connectivity signal was confirmed for several pathways and processes, including autophagy and MTOR signaling (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).

claim: Screening of the mini-pool in H4 Cas9 GFP-SQSTM1 cells showed a high confirmation rate when the top-ranked hits from the primary screen were analyzed.

claim: The MTOR and autophagy pathways are key regulators of SQSTM1.
source: Similar to the GFP assay, we used FACS to isolate a high and low cell population based on the SQSTM1 staining intensity. This approach confirmed that the MTOR and autophagy pathways are key regulators of SQSTM1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the mini-pool screen with endogenous SQSTM1 staining.

claim: Components of the mediator complex failed to robustly score in the endogenous SQSTM1 mini-pool screen.
source: However, components of the mediator complex or targets linked to translation such as SBDS and DPH1 failed to robustly score which suggests that these specifically regulate the GFP-SQSTM1 reporter (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F and G.

claim: Targets linked to translation such as SBDS and DPH1 failed to robustly score in the endogenous SQSTM1 mini-pool screen.
source: However, components of the mediator complex or targets linked to translation such as SBDS and DPH1 failed to robustly score which suggests that these specifically regulate the GFP-SQSTM1 reporter (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F and G.

claim: Mediator complex components and translation-linked targets specifically regulate the GFP-SQSTM1 reporter.
source: However, components of the mediator complex or targets linked to translation such as SBDS and DPH1 failed to robustly score which suggests that these specifically regulate the GFP-SQSTM1 reporter (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This is inferred from the differential results between GFP-SQSTM1 and endogenous SQSTM1 screens.

claim: sgRNAs against HNRNPM, SLC39A14, SRRD and PGK1 were enriched in cells displaying high levels of both GFP-SQSTM1 and endogenous SQSTM1.
source: sgRNAs against HNRNPM, SLC39A14, SRRD and PGK1 were enriched in cells displaying high levels of both GFP-SQSTM1 and endogenous SQSTM1 (Figure 3A), and to our knowledge, these candidates have not been linked to the regulation of SQSTM1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: HNRNPM, SLC39A14, SRRD and PGK1 have not been linked to the regulation of SQSTM1.
source: sgRNAs against HNRNPM, SLC39A14, SRRD and PGK1 were enriched in cells displaying high levels of both GFP-SQSTM1 and endogenous SQSTM1 (Figure 3A), and to our knowledge, these candidates have not been linked to the regulation of SQSTM1.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the findings based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: Individual sgRNAs against HNRNPM, SLC39A14, SRRD and PGK1 caused a robust increase in SQSTM1 levels by immunoblot.
source: When these sgRNAs were individually tested in H4 Cas9 cells, we observed a robust increase in SQSTM1 levels by immunoblot, similar to the depletion of ATG7 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: UFM1 and components of its conjugation machinery scored as modulators of endogenous and GFP-tagged SQSTM1.
source: We also noticed that ubiquitin-fold modifier 1 (UFM1) and components of its conjugation machinery scored as modulators of endogenous and GFP-tagged SQSTM1 (Figure 3A).

claim: UFM1 is a ubiquitin-like molecule which is post-translationally processed by UFM1-specific proteases (UFSP1 and UFSP2).
source: UFM1 is a ubiquitin-like molecule which is post-translationally processed by UFM1-specific proteases (UFSP1 and UFSP2) and then conjugated to target proteins via the ubiquitin-like modifier activating enzyme 5 (UBA5), ubiquitin-fold modifier conjugating enzyme 1 (UFC1) and the UFM1-specific ligase (UFL1) (Figure 3C) (Daniel and Liebau, 2014; Komatsu et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a description of the ufmylation pathway supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: UFM1 is conjugated to target proteins via the ubiquitin-like modifier activating enzyme 5 (UBA5), ubiquitin-fold modifier conjugating enzyme 1 (UFC1) and the UFM1-specific ligase (UFL1).
source: UFM1 is a ubiquitin-like molecule which is post-translationally processed by UFM1-specific proteases (UFSP1 and UFSP2) and then conjugated to target proteins via the ubiquitin-like modifier activating enzyme 5 (UBA5), ubiquitin-fold modifier conjugating enzyme 1 (UFC1) and the UFM1-specific ligase (UFL1) (Figure 3C) (Daniel and Liebau, 2014; Komatsu et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a description of the ufmylation pathway supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Protein ufmylation was exposed in the primary screen as one of the most significantly enriched biological processes in GFP-SQSTM1 high cells.
source: Protein ufmylation was already exposed in the primary screen as one of the most significantly enriched biological processes in GFP-SQSTM1 high cells (Figure 2D) and all components of the cascade scored with the exception of UFSP1.
evidence: This claim is supported by enrichment analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: All components of the ufmylation cascade scored in the primary screen with the exception of UFSP1.
source: Protein ufmylation was already exposed in the primary screen as one of the most significantly enriched biological processes in GFP-SQSTM1 high cells (Figure 2D) and all components of the cascade scored with the exception of UFSP1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the genome-wide screen.

claim: Ufmylation has been implicated in the control of cell differentiation, growth and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis.
source: Ufmylation has been implicated in the control of cell differentiation, growth and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis (Daniel and Liebau, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Knockout of the murine homolog of UFL1 has been linked to impaired autophagy.
source: Knockout of the murine homolog of UFL1 has been linked to impaired autophagy (Zhang et al., 2015), but the role of ufmylation in the autophagic process is controversial (Cai et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The role of ufmylation in the autophagic process is controversial.

claim: Individual sgRNAs against UFM1, UBA5, UFL1, UFC1 and UFSP2 confirmed efficient depletion of the corresponding target proteins.

claim: Individual sgRNAs against UFM1, UBA5, UFL1, UFC1 and UFSP2 caused robust accumulation of GFP-SQSTM1 and endogenous SQSTM1.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3D-F.

claim: Depletion of UFM1 increased SQSTM1.
source: Depletion of UFM1 increased SQSTM1 and slightly augmented the levels of the autophagy cargo receptors CALCOCO2 (also known as NDP52) and TAX1BP1; however, levels of LC3-I and LC3-II appeared largely unchanged (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Depletion of UFM1 slightly augmented the levels of the autophagy cargo receptors CALCOCO2 and TAX1BP1.
source: Depletion of UFM1 increased SQSTM1 and slightly augmented the levels of the autophagy cargo receptors CALCOCO2 (also known as NDP52) and TAX1BP1; however, levels of LC3-I and LC3-II appeared largely unchanged (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: CALCOCO2 is also known as NDP52.
source: Depletion of UFM1 increased SQSTM1 and slightly augmented the levels of the autophagy cargo receptors CALCOCO2 (also known as NDP52) and TAX1BP1; however, levels of LC3-I and LC3-II appeared largely unchanged (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a nomenclature statement based on established knowledge.

claim: Levels of LC3-I and LC3-II appeared largely unchanged upon UFM1 depletion.
source: Depletion of UFM1 increased SQSTM1 and slightly augmented the levels of the autophagy cargo receptors CALCOCO2 (also known as NDP52) and TAX1BP1; however, levels of LC3-I and LC3-II appeared largely unchanged (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: UFM1-depleted cells were as sensitive to the V-ATPase inhibitor Bafilomycin A1 as the control cells.
source: UFM1-depleted cells were as sensitive to the V-ATPase inhibitor Bafilomycin A1 as the control cells suggesting that autophagic flux of LC3 is unchanged (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Autophagic flux of LC3 is unchanged in UFM1-depleted cells.
source: UFM1-depleted cells were as sensitive to the V-ATPase inhibitor Bafilomycin A1 as the control cells suggesting that autophagic flux of LC3 is unchanged (Figure 4A).
